// packages/database/src/entities/permission.entity.ts

import { Entity, Column, ManyToMany, Index, Unique } from "typeorm";
import { BaseEntity } from "./base.entity";
import { Role } from "./role.entity";

/**
 * Permission Entity
 *
 * Defines granular permissions for actions on resources.
 * Format: resource:action (e.g., users:read, clients:write)
 *
 * Permissions are tenant-scoped.
 */
@Entity("permissions")
@Unique(["tenantId", "name"])
@Index(["tenantId"])
@Index(["resource"])
@Index(["action"])
export class Permission extends BaseEntity {
  // ============================================================
  // TENANT RELATIONSHIP
  // ============================================================

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "tenant_id" })
  @Index()
  tenantId!: string;

  // ============================================================
  // PERMISSION DETAILS
  // ============================================================

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 100,
    unique: false, // Unique per tenant via composite index
    comment: "Permission name (e.g., users:read)",
  })
  name!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 50,
    comment: "Resource type (e.g., users, clients, api)",
  })
  resource!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 50,
    comment: "Action (e.g., read, write, delete, manage, *)",
  })
  action!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "text",
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Human-readable description",
  })
  description?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 50,
    default: "tenant",
    comment: "Scope level: platform, tenant, user",
  })
  scope!: string;

  // ============================================================
  // METADATA
  // ============================================================

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",
    default: false,
    name: "is_system",
    comment: "System permission (cannot be deleted)",
  })
  isSystem!: boolean;

  @Column({
    type: "jsonb",
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Additional metadata (conditions, constraints, etc.)",
  })
  metadata?: {
    conditions?: string[]; // e.g., ["own_resource_only"]
    constraints?: Record<string, any>;
  };

  // ============================================================
  // RELATIONSHIPS
  // ============================================================

  @ManyToMany(() => Role, (role) => role.permissions)
  roles!: Role[];

  // ============================================================
  // HELPER METHODS
  // ============================================================

  /**
   * Get resource from permission name
   * users:read → users
   */
  static getResource(permissionName: string): string {
    return permissionName.split(":")[0] as string;
  }

  /**
   * Get action from permission name
   * users:read → read
   */
  static getAction(permissionName: string): string {
    return permissionName.split(":")[1] as string;
  }

  /**
   * Parse permission name into components
   */
  static parse(permissionName: string): { resource: string; action: string } {
    const [resource, action] = permissionName.split(":") as [string, string];
    return { resource, action };
  }

  /**
   * Check if permission matches pattern
   * users:read matches users:* or *:read or *:*
   */
  matches(pattern: string): boolean {
    const [patternResource, patternAction] = pattern.split(":");

    // Exact match
    if (this.name === pattern) {
      return true;
    }

    // Wildcard resource (*:read)
    if (patternResource === "*" && this.action === patternAction) {
      return true;
    }

    // Wildcard action (users:*)
    if (this.resource === patternResource && patternAction === "*") {
      return true;
    }

    // Full wildcard (*:*)
    if (patternResource === "*" && patternAction === "*") {
      return true;
    }

    return false;
  }

  /**
   * Check if this permission implies another permission
   * users:* implies users:read
   */
  implies(permission: Permission): boolean {
    // Same permission
    if (this.name === permission.name) {
      return true;
    }

    // Same resource, this has wildcard action
    if (this.resource === permission.resource && this.action === "*") {
      return true;
    }

    // This has full wildcard
    if (this.resource === "*" && this.action === "*") {
      return true;
    }

    return false;
  }

  /**
   * Get full permission name
   */
  get fullName(): string {
    return this.name;
  }

  /**
   * Check if this is a wildcard permission
   */
  get isWildcard(): boolean {
    return this.resource === "*" || this.action === "*";
  }
}

import {
  Entity,
  Column,
  ManyToMany,
  JoinTable,
  Index,
  Unique,
  OneToMany,
} from "typeorm";
import { BaseEntity } from "./base.entity";
import { Permission } from "./permission.entity";
import { User } from "./user.entity";
import { RolePermission } from "./role-permission.entity";

/**
 * Role Entity
 *
 * Groups permissions into named roles.
 * Users are assigned roles, roles grant permissions.
 *
 * Roles are tenant-scoped.
 */
@Entity("roles")
@Unique(["tenantId", "name"])
@Index(["tenantId"])
@Index(["isSystem"])
export class Role extends BaseEntity {
  // ============================================================
  // TENANT RELATIONSHIP
  // ============================================================

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "tenant_id" })
  tenantId!: string;

  // ============================================================
  // ROLE DETAILS
  // ============================================================

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 100,
    unique: false, // Unique per tenant via composite index
    comment: "Role name (e.g., admin, developer, user)",
  })
  name!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,
    nullable: true,
    name: "display_name",
    comment: "Human-readable display name",
  })
  displayName?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "text",
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Role description",
  })
  description?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 50,
    default: "tenant",
    comment: "Scope level: platform, tenant, custom",
  })
  scope!: string;

  // ============================================================
  // FLAGS
  // ============================================================

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",
    default: false,
    name: "is_system",
    comment: "System role (cannot be deleted or modified)",
  })
  isSystem!: boolean;

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",
    default: true,
    name: "is_active",
    comment: "Whether this role is active",
  })
  isActive!: boolean;

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",
    default: false,
    name: "is_default",
    comment: "Automatically assigned to new users",
  })
  isDefault!: boolean;

  // ============================================================
  // METADATA
  // ============================================================

  @Column({
    type: "integer",
    default: 0,
    comment: "Higher priority = more powerful (for conflict resolution)",
  })
  priority!: number;

  @Column({
    type: "jsonb",
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Additional metadata",
  })
  metadata?: {
    color?: string;
    icon?: string;
    maxUsers?: number;
    features?: string[];
  };

  @Column({
    type: "uuid",
    nullable: true,
    name: "created_by",
    comment: "User who created this role",
  })
  createdBy?: string;

  // ============================================================
  // RELATIONSHIPS
  // ============================================================

  // Many-to-Many via explicit RolePermission entity
  // NO @JoinTable - we have explicit RolePermission entity with metadata
  @ManyToMany(() => Permission, (permission) => permission.roles)
  permissions!: Permission[];

  @ManyToMany(() => User, (user) => user.roles)
  users!: User[];

  // OneToMany to access join table metadata
  @OneToMany(() => RolePermission, (rp) => rp.role)
  rolePermissions!: RolePermission[];

  // ============================================================
  // HELPER METHODS
  // ============================================================

  /**
   * Check if role has a specific permission
   */
  hasPermission(permissionName: string): boolean {
    if (!this.permissions) {
      return false;
    }

    return this.permissions.some((permission) => {
      // Exact match
      if (permission.name === permissionName) {
        return true;
      }

      // Check if permission implies the requested one
      const [resource, action] = permissionName.split(":");

      // Permission with wildcard action (users:*)
      if (permission.resource === resource && permission.action === "*") {
        return true;
      }

      // Full wildcard (*:*)
      if (permission.resource === "*" && permission.action === "*") {
        return true;
      }

      return false;
    });
  }

  /**
   * Check if role has any of the permissions
   */
  hasAnyPermission(permissionNames: string[]): boolean {
    return permissionNames.some((name) => this.hasPermission(name));
  }

  /**
   * Check if role has all permissions
   */
  hasAllPermissions(permissionNames: string[]): boolean {
    return permissionNames.every((name) => this.hasPermission(name));
  }

  /**
   * Get all permission names for this role
   */
  getPermissionNames(): string[] {
    if (!this.permissions) {
      return [];
    }
    return this.permissions.map((p) => p.name);
  }

  /**
   * Get permissions grouped by resource
   */
  getPermissionsByResource(): Record<string, string[]> {
    if (!this.permissions) {
      return {};
    }

    const grouped: Record<string, string[]> = {};

    for (const permission of this.permissions) {
      if (!grouped[permission.resource]) {
        grouped[permission.resource] = [];
      }
      // @ts-ignore
      grouped[permission.resource].push(permission.action);
    }

    return grouped;
  }

  /**
   * Check if this is an admin role
   */
  get isAdmin(): boolean {
    return (
      this.name === "admin" ||
      this.name === "super_admin" ||
      this.hasPermission("*:*")
    );
  }

  /**
   * Check if this role can be modified
   */
  get isModifiable(): boolean {
    return !this.isSystem;
  }

  /**
   * Check if this role can be deleted
   */
  get isDeletable(): boolean {
    return !this.isSystem && !this.isDefault;
  }
}

/**

 *
 * Logs all security-related events:
 * - Login attempts (success/failure)
 * - Password changes
 * - MFA events
 * - Account lockouts

@Index(["tenantId"])

@Index(["severity"])
@Index(["createdAt"])
@Index(["ipAddress"])
export class SecurityEvent extends BaseEntity {

  @ManyToOne(() => User, {
    onDelete: "SET NULL",
    nullable: true,
  })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "user_id" })
  user?: User;

  @Column({ type: "uuid", nullable: true, name: "tenant_id" })
  tenantId?: string;

  // ON DELETE SET NULL — audit logs must survive tenant deletion for compliance.
  @ManyToOne(() => Tenant, {
    onDelete: "SET NULL",
    nullable: true,
  })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "tenant_id" })
  tenant?: Tenant;

    length: 100,
    name: "event_type",

  eventType!: string;

  @Column({

    length: 45,

  })

  @Column({

  deviceInfo?: Record<string, any>;

  @Column({
    type: "jsonb",
    default: {},

  })
  metadata!: Record<string, any>;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Geographic location",
  })
  location?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",

  })
  isAnomaly!: boolean;

  /**

   */

    nullable: true,

    comment: "Denormalized actor email at event time — survives user deletion",
  })
  actorEmail?: string;

  })

  @Column({

    name: "resource_id",

  @Column({

@Entity("social_link_requests")
@Index(["token"], { unique: true })
@Index(["tenantId", "userId"])
export class SocialLinkRequest extends BaseEntity {
  // ============================================================
  // RELATIONSHIPS
  // ============================================================

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "tenant_id" })
  tenantId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => Tenant, { onDelete: "CASCADE" })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "tenant_id" })
  tenant!: Tenant;

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "user_id" })
  userId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => User, { onDelete: "CASCADE" })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "user_id" })
  user!: User;

  // ============================================================
  // REQUEST DATA
  // ============================================================

    type: "varchar",
    length: 50,

    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,
    name: "provider_id",
  })
  providerId!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,
    name: "provider_email",
  })
  providerEmail!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,
    unique: true,
    comment: "Verification token sent via email",
  })
  token!: string;

  @Column({
    type: "jsonb",
    comment: "Social profile data to be linked",
  })
  profileData!: {
    displayName?: string;
    avatarUrl?: string;
    accessToken: string;
    refreshToken?: string;
    tokenExpiresAt?: Date;
    scopes?: string;
    metadata?: Record<string, any>;
  };

  @Column({
    type: "timestamp with time zone",
    name: "expires_at",
    comment: "When this request expires",
  })
  expiresAt!: Date;

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",
    default: false,
    comment: "Has this request been completed?",
  })
  completed!: boolean;

  @Column({
    type: "timestamp with time zone",
    nullable: true,
    name: "completed_at",
  })
  completedAt?: Date;

  @Column({
    type: "inet",
    nullable: true,
    name: "ip_address",
  })
  ipAddress?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "text",
    nullable: true,
    name: "user_agent",
  })
  userAgent?: string;

  // ============================================================
  // HELPERS
  // ============================================================

  get isExpired(): boolean {
    return this.expiresAt < new Date();
  }

  get isValid(): boolean {
    return !this.completed && !this.isExpired;
  }
}

import { Entity, Column, ManyToOne, JoinColumn, Index, Unique } from "typeorm";
import { BaseEntity } from "./base.entity";
import { User } from "./user.entity";
import { Role } from "./role.entity";

/**
 * UserRole Entity (Join Table)
 *
 * Explicit join table for User-Role many-to-many relationship.
 * Allows additional metadata like assignment date, expiry, etc.
 */
@Entity("user_roles")
@Unique(["userId", "roleId"])
@Index(["userId"])
@Index(["roleId"])
@Index(["tenantId"])
@Index(["expiresAt"])
export class UserRole extends BaseEntity {
  // PRIMARY KEY - must be explicitly marked
  // This tells TypeORM this is NOT a simple join table

  // ============================================================
  // TENANT RELATIONSHIP
  // ============================================================

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "tenant_id" })
  tenantId!: string;

  // ============================================================
  // RELATIONSHIPS
  // ============================================================

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "user_id" })
  userId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => User, (user) => user.userRoles, {
    onDelete: "CASCADE",
  })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "user_id" })
  user!: User;

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "role_id" })
  roleId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => Role, (role) => role.users, {
    onDelete: "CASCADE",
  })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "role_id" })
  role!: Role;

  // ============================================================
  // METADATA
  // ============================================================

  @Column({
    type: "uuid",
    nullable: true,
    name: "assigned_by",
    comment: "User who assigned this role",
  })
  assignedBy?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "timestamp",
    nullable: true,
    name: "assigned_at",
    default: () => "CURRENT_TIMESTAMP",
    comment: "When role was assigned",
  })
  assignedAt!: Date;

  @Column({
    type: "timestamp",
    nullable: true,
    name: "expires_at",
    comment: "When role assignment expires (null = permanent)",
  })
  expiresAt?: Date;

  @Column({
    type: "text",
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Reason for assignment",
  })
  reason?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "jsonb",
    nullable: true,
    comment: "Additional metadata (conditions, restrictions, etc.)",
  })
  metadata?: {
    conditions?: string[];
    restrictions?: Record<string, any>;
    source?: string; // 'manual', 'auto', 'sso', etc.
  };

  // ============================================================
  // HELPER METHODS
  // ============================================================

  /**
   * Check if role assignment is expired
   */
  get isExpired(): boolean {
    if (!this.expiresAt) {
      return false;
    }
    return this.expiresAt < new Date();
  }

  /**
   * Check if role assignment is active
   */
  get isActive(): boolean {
    return !this.isExpired;
  }

  /**
   * Get days until expiry
   */
  get daysUntilExpiry(): number | null {
    if (!this.expiresAt) {
      return null;
    }
    const now = new Date();
    const diff = this.expiresAt.getTime() - now.getTime();
    return Math.ceil(diff / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24));
  }

  /**
   * Check if assignment is permanent
   */
  get isPermanent(): boolean {
    return !this.expiresAt;
  }
}

  // ============================================================
  // HELPERS
  // ============================================================

  get isTokenExpired(): boolean {
    if (!this.tokenExpiresAt) return false;
    return this.tokenExpiresAt < new Date();
  }

  get scopesList(): string[] {
    if (!this.scopes) return [];
    return this.scopes.split(" ").filter(Boolean);
  }
}

import {
  Entity,
  Column,
  Index,
  ManyToOne,
  OneToOne,
  OneToMany,
  ManyToMany,

  JoinTable,
} from "typeorm";

@Entity("users")
@Index(["tenantId", "email"], { unique: true })
@Index(["email"])
@Index(["tenantId"])
@Index(["status"])
@Index(["emailVerified"])
@Index(["lastLoginAt"])
export class User extends BaseEntity {
  // Tenant relation

    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,

    nullable: true,

    type: "varchar",

  passwordHistory!: string[];

    comment: "User account status",

  status!: "active" | "inactive" | "suspended" | "deleted";

  failedLoginAttempts!: number;

  passwordResetExpiresAt?: Date;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 255,
    nullable: true,
    name: "magic_link_token",
    select: false,
    comment: "SHA-256 hash of the magic link token",
  })
  magicLinkToken?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "timestamp with time zone",
    nullable: true,
    name: "magic_link_expires_at",
  })
  magicLinkExpiresAt?: Date;

  @Column({
    type: "jsonb",
    default: {},
    comment: "Additional user metadata",
  })
  metadata?: Record<string, any>;

  @Column({
    type: "varchar",
    length: 10,
    nullable: true,
    comment: "User timezone (e.g., America/New_York)",
  })
  timezone?: string;

  @Column({
    type: "boolean",
    default: true,
    name: "is_active",
  })
  isActive!: boolean;

  // Relationships
  @OneToOne(() => MfaSettings, (mfa) => mfa.user, { cascade: true })
  mfaSettings?: MfaSettings;

  @OneToMany(() => Session, (session) => session.user)
  sessions!: Session[];

  // ============================================================
  // RBAC RELATIONSHIPS - NEW
  // ============================================================

  // Many-to-Many via explicit UserRole entity
  // NO @JoinTable - we have explicit UserRole entity with metadata
  @ManyToMany(() => Role, (role) => role.users)
  roles!: Role[];

  // OneToMany to access join table metadata
  @OneToMany(() => UserRole, (userRole) => userRole.user)
  userRoles!: UserRole[];

  @Column({
    type: 'varchar',
    length: 50,
    nullable: true,
    name: 'preferred_auth_method',
    comment: 'User preferred authentication method',
  })
  preferredAuthMethod?:
    | 'password'
    | 'magicLink'
    | 'passkey'
    | 'social';

  // ⭐ NEW: MFA enabled flag
  @Column({
    type: 'boolean',
    default: false,
    name: 'mfa_enabled',
    comment: 'Whether user has enabled MFA',
  })
  mfaEnabled!: boolean;

  // ============================================================
  // RBAC HELPER METHODS - NEW
  // ============================================================

  /**
   * Check if user has a specific role
   */
  hasRole(roleName: string): boolean {
    if (!this.roles) {
      return false;
    }
    return this.roles.some((role) => role.name === roleName);
  }

  /**
   * Check if user has any of the roles
   */
  hasAnyRole(roleNames: string[]): boolean {
    return roleNames.some((name) => this.hasRole(name));
  }

  /**
   * Check if user has all roles
   */
  hasAllRoles(roleNames: string[]): boolean {
    return roleNames.every((name) => this.hasRole(name));
  }

  /**
   * Check if user has a specific permission
   */
  hasPermission(permissionName: string): boolean {
    if (!this.roles) {
      return false;
    }
    return this.roles.some((role) => role.hasPermission(permissionName));
  }

  /**
   * Check if user has any of the permissions
   */
  hasAnyPermission(permissionNames: string[]): boolean {
    return permissionNames.some((name) => this.hasPermission(name));
  }

  /**
   * Check if user has all permissions
   */
  hasAllPermissions(permissionNames: string[]): boolean {
    return permissionNames.every((name) => this.hasPermission(name));
  }

  /**
   * Get all permission names for this user
   */
  getPermissions(): string[] {
    if (!this.roles) {
      return [];
    }

    const permissions = new Set<string>();

    for (const role of this.roles) {
      const rolePermissions = role.getPermissionNames();
      rolePermissions.forEach((p) => permissions.add(p));
    }

    return Array.from(permissions);
  }

  /**
   * Get all role names for this user
   */
  getRoleNames(): string[] {
    if (!this.roles) {
      return [];
    }
    return this.roles.map((r) => r.name);
  }

  /**
   * Check if user is admin (has admin role or admin permissions)
   */
  get isAdmin(): boolean {
    if (!this.roles) {
      return false;
    }
    return this.roles.some((role) => role.isAdmin);
  }

  /**
   * Get highest priority role
   */
  get primaryRole(): Role | undefined {
    if (!this.roles || this.roles.length === 0) {
      return undefined;
    }
    return this.roles.sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority)[0];
  }

  /**
   * Check if user has expired role assignments
   */
  hasExpiredRoles(): boolean {
    if (!this.userRoles) {
      return false;
    }
    return this.userRoles.some((ur) => ur.isExpired);
  }

  // ============================================================
  // EXISTING HELPER METHODS
  // ============================================================

  get fullName(): string {
    if (this.firstName && this.lastName) {
      return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`;
    }
    return this.displayName || this.email;
  }

  get isLocked(): boolean {
    if (!this.lockedUntil) return false;
    return new Date() < this.lockedUntil;
  }
}

/**
 * WebAuthn Credential Entity
 *
 * Stores registered FIDO2/passkey credentials for users.
 * One row per credential (device). Replaces the jsonb[] column
 * that previously lived on mfa_settings.
 */
@Entity("webauthn_credentials")
@Index(["tenantId", "credentialId"], { unique: true })
export class WebAuthnCredential {
  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn("uuid")
  id!: string;

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "user_id" })
  userId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => User, { onDelete: "CASCADE" })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "user_id" })
  user!: User;

  @Column({ type: "uuid", name: "tenant_id" })
  tenantId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => Tenant, { onDelete: "CASCADE" })
  @JoinColumn({ name: "tenant_id" })
  tenant!: Tenant;

  /** Base64URL-encoded credential ID as returned by the authenticator */
  @Column({ type: "text", name: "credential_id" })
  credentialId!: string;

  /** Raw COSE public-key bytes */
  @Column({ type: "bytea", name: "public_key" })
  publicKey!: Buffer;

  @Column({ type: "integer", name: "counter", default: 0 })
  counter!: number;

  @Column({ type: "varchar", length: 255, name: "device_name", nullable: true })
  deviceName?: string;

  @Column({ type: "text", array: true, name: "transports", nullable: true })
  transports?: string[];

  @Column({
    type: "timestamp with time zone",
    name: "last_used_at",
    nullable: true,
  })
  lastUsedAt?: Date;

  @CreateDateColumn({
    type: "timestamp with time zone",
    name: "created_at",
  })
  createdAt!: Date;
}

      ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE;

    // ============================================

      WHERE slug IS NULL;

    // Ensure all slugs are unique by appending numbers if needed
    await queryRunner.query(`
      WITH duplicates AS (
        SELECT id, slug, 
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY slug ORDER BY created_at) as rn
        FROM tenants
      )
      UPDATE tenants t
      SET slug = d.slug || '-' || d.rn
      FROM duplicates d
      WHERE t.id = d.id AND d.rn > 1;
    `);

    // ============================================
    // Step 3: Make slug NOT NULL after population
    // ============================================
    await queryRunner.query(`
      ALTER TABLE tenants

    // ============================================

    // ============================================
    await queryRunner.query(`

          active = TRUE
      WHERE environment IS NULL OR active IS NULL;
    `);
  }

import { MigrationInterface, QueryRunner } from "typeorm";

/**
 * HardenSecurityEventAudit
 *
 * 1. Adds actor_email, application_id, resource_id, resource_type columns.
 * 2. Changes security_events.tenant_id FK from ON DELETE CASCADE → ON DELETE SET NULL
 *    so audit records survive tenant deletion (compliance requirement).
 * 3. Adds a soft FK to oauth_clients for application_id (ON DELETE SET NULL).
 */
export class HardenSecurityEventAudit1735500000000
  implements MigrationInterface
{
  name = "HardenSecurityEventAudit1735500000000";

  public async up(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    console.log("🔒 HardenSecurityEventAudit: starting migration…");

    // ── 1. New audit columns ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    await queryRunner.query(`
      ALTER TABLE security_events
        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS actor_email    VARCHAR(255),
        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS application_id UUID,
        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS resource_id    VARCHAR(255),
        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS resource_type  VARCHAR(50);
    `);

    console.log(
      "  ✅ Added actor_email, application_id, resource_id, resource_type",
    );

    // ── 2. Change tenant_id FK: CASCADE → SET NULL ────────────────────────
    //
    // We need to:
    //  a) Find the existing FK constraint name (it may vary per installation).
    //  b) Drop it.
    //  c) Recreate it with ON DELETE SET NULL.

    const fkRows: Array<{ constraint_name: string }> = await queryRunner.query(`
        SELECT tc.constraint_name
        FROM   information_schema.table_constraints    tc
        JOIN   information_schema.key_column_usage     kcu
               ON tc.constraint_name = kcu.constraint_name
               AND tc.table_schema   = kcu.table_schema
        JOIN   information_schema.referential_constraints rc
               ON tc.constraint_name = rc.constraint_name
               AND tc.table_schema   = rc.constraint_schema
        WHERE  tc.constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY'
          AND  tc.table_name      = 'security_events'
          AND  kcu.column_name    = 'tenant_id';
      `);

    if (fkRows.length > 0) {
      const fkName = fkRows[0]?.constraint_name;
      console.log(`  ⚙️  Dropping existing tenant_id FK: ${fkName}`);
      await queryRunner.query(
        `ALTER TABLE security_events DROP CONSTRAINT "${fkName}";`,
      );
    }

import { MigrationInterface, QueryRunner } from "typeorm";

/**
 * Migration: AddWebAuthnCredentialsTable
 *
 * 1. Creates dedicated `webauthn_credentials` table.
 * 2. Migrates existing JSONB credentials from `mfa_settings.webauthn_credentials`.
 * 3. Drops the `webauthn_credentials` JSONB column from `mfa_settings`.
 */
export class AddWebAuthnCredentialsTable1773700000000
  implements MigrationInterface
{
  name = "AddWebAuthnCredentialsTable1773700000000";

  public async up(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Create the new table
    await queryRunner.query(`
      CREATE TABLE "webauthn_credentials" (
        "id"            UUID          NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
        "user_id"       UUID          NOT NULL,
        "tenant_id"     UUID          NOT NULL,
        "credential_id" TEXT          NOT NULL,
        "public_key"    BYTEA         NOT NULL,
        "counter"       INTEGER       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        "device_name"   VARCHAR(255),
        "transports"    TEXT[],
        "last_used_at"  TIMESTAMPTZ,
        "created_at"    TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
        CONSTRAINT "PK_webauthn_credentials" PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
        CONSTRAINT "FK_webauthn_credentials_user"
          FOREIGN KEY ("user_id") REFERENCES "users"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
        CONSTRAINT "FK_webauthn_credentials_tenant"
          FOREIGN KEY ("tenant_id") REFERENCES "tenants"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
        CONSTRAINT "UQ_webauthn_credentials_tenant_credential"
          UNIQUE ("tenant_id", "credential_id")
      );
    `);

    await queryRunner.query(`
      CREATE INDEX "IDX_webauthn_credentials_user_tenant"
        ON "webauthn_credentials" ("user_id", "tenant_id");
    `);

    // 2. Migrate existing JSONB credentials from mfa_settings
    //    Each element in the jsonb array becomes one row.
    //    public_key is stored as base64url string in JSONB → convert to bytea.
    await queryRunner.query(`
      INSERT INTO "webauthn_credentials"
        ("user_id", "tenant_id", "credential_id", "public_key",
         "counter", "device_name", "transports", "last_used_at", "created_at")
      SELECT
        ms."user_id",
        ms."tenant_id",
        cred->>'id'                                        AS credential_id,
        decode(
          regexp_replace(
            regexp_replace(cred->>'publicKey', '-', '+', 'g'),
            '_', '/', 'g'
          ) || repeat('=', (4 - length(cred->>'publicKey') % 4) % 4),
          'base64'
        )                                                  AS public_key,
        COALESCE((cred->>'counter')::integer, 0)           AS counter,
        cred->>'deviceName'                                AS device_name,
        ARRAY(
          SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(COALESCE(cred->'transports', '[]'::jsonb))
        )                                                  AS transports,
        (cred->>'lastUsedAt')::timestamptz                 AS last_used_at,
        COALESCE((cred->>'createdAt')::timestamptz, NOW()) AS created_at
      FROM "mfa_settings" ms,
           jsonb_array_elements(
             CASE
               WHEN ms."webauthn_credentials" IS NULL
                 OR jsonb_typeof(ms."webauthn_credentials") = 'null'
               THEN '[]'::jsonb
               ELSE ms."webauthn_credentials"
             END
           ) AS cred
      WHERE jsonb_typeof(
              CASE
                WHEN ms."webauthn_credentials" IS NULL
                THEN '[]'::jsonb
                ELSE ms."webauthn_credentials"
              END
            ) = 'array'
        AND jsonb_array_length(
              CASE
                WHEN ms."webauthn_credentials" IS NULL
                THEN '[]'::jsonb
                ELSE ms."webauthn_credentials"
              END
            ) > 0
      ON CONFLICT ("tenant_id", "credential_id") DO NOTHING;
    `);

    // 3. Drop the JSONB column from mfa_settings
    await queryRunner.query(`
      ALTER TABLE "mfa_settings" DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS "webauthn_credentials";
    `);
  }

  public async down(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    // Re-add the JSONB column
    await queryRunner.query(`
      ALTER TABLE "mfa_settings"
        ADD COLUMN "webauthn_credentials" JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]';
    `);

    // Restore data from the dedicated table back into JSONB
    await queryRunner.query(`
      WITH agg AS (
        SELECT
          wc."user_id",
          wc."tenant_id",
          jsonb_agg(
            jsonb_build_object(
              'id',          wc."credential_id",
              'publicKey',   encode(wc."public_key", 'base64'),
              'counter',     wc."counter",
              'deviceName',  wc."device_name",
              'transports',  to_jsonb(wc."transports"),
              'lastUsedAt',  wc."last_used_at",
              'createdAt',   wc."created_at"
            )
          ) AS credentials
        FROM "webauthn_credentials" wc
        GROUP BY wc."user_id", wc."tenant_id"
      )
      UPDATE "mfa_settings" ms
      SET "webauthn_credentials" = agg.credentials
      FROM agg
      WHERE ms."user_id"   = agg."user_id"
        AND ms."tenant_id" = agg."tenant_id";
    `);

    // Drop the dedicated table
    await queryRunner.query(`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "webauthn_credentials";`);
  }
}

/**
 * Adds security-hardening columns to the sessions table:
 *   - access_token_hash   : SHA-256 of the last issued access JWT (never raw token)
 *   - refresh_expires_at  : expiry of the active refresh token (updated on rotation)
 *   - last_used_at        : timestamp set on every successful refresh rotation
 *
 * Also creates a composite index on (expires_at, revoked_at) to accelerate the
 * 15-minute cleanup query:  WHERE expires_at < NOW() AND revoked_at IS NULL
 */
export class AddSessionSecurityFields1780000000000 implements MigrationInterface {
  name = "AddSessionSecurityFields1780000000000";

  public async up(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    // New columns
    await queryRunner.query(`

        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "access_token_hash"  VARCHAR(255)              DEFAULT NULL,
        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "refresh_expires_at" TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE  DEFAULT NULL,
        ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "last_used_at"       TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE  DEFAULT NULL
    `);

    // Composite index for the cleanup query
    await queryRunner.query(`
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "IDX_sessions_expires_at_revoked_at"
        ON "sessions" ("expires_at", "revoked_at")
    `);
  }

  public async down(queryRunner: QueryRunner): Promise<void> {
    await queryRunner.query(

      ALTER TABLE "sessions"
        DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS "last_used_at",
        DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS "refresh_expires_at",
        DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS "access_token_hash"
    `);

# 🏰 Fort Knox SDK

**Enterprise-grade authentication SDK for multi-tenant applications**

Built on the principles of Auth0, Clerk, and NextAuth - but for your own infrastructure.

---

## 🎯 Design Principles

1. **Access tokens live in memory** (never localStorage)
2. **Refresh tokens live in httpOnly cookies** (XSS-safe)
3. **SDK never stores refresh tokens** (cookies handle it)
4. **SDK only refreshes on 401** (no refresh storms)
5. **Concurrency-safe refresh** (single refresh, queue requests)
6. **Environment-agnostic** (works everywhere)

---

## 📦 Installation

```bash
npm install @fortknox/sdk
# or
yarn add @fortknox/sdk
# or
pnpm add @fortknox/sdk
```

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### **Browser / React**

```typescript
import { createWebClient } from '@fortknox/sdk';
import { FortKnoxProvider, useAuth } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';

// Create client
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'http://localhost:4000',
  tenant: 'acme',
  debug: true,
});

// Wrap app
function App() {
  return (
    <FortKnoxProvider client={client}>
      <YourApp />
    </FortKnoxProvider>
  );
}

// Use in components
function LoginPage() {
  const { login, user, isAuthenticated } = useAuth();

  const handleLogin = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    await login({ email, password });
  };

  if (isAuthenticated) {
    return <div>Welcome {user?.email}!</div>;
  }

  return <form onSubmit={handleLogin}>...</form>;
}
```

```
@fortknox/sdk
├── /core        Pure auth logic (works everywhere)
├── /web         Browser helpers
├── /react       React hooks
├── /next        Next.js SSR
└── /node        Server-to-server
```

### **1. Browser (Vanilla JS)**

```typescript
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.scrolloop.com',
  tenant: 'acme',
});

// Login

// Get user

// Logout
await client.logout();
```

### **2. React**

```typescript

// In component

  const { user, isLoading } = useUser();
  
  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>;
  return <div>Hello {user?.email}</div>;
}
```

### **3. Next.js (Server Components)**

```typescript
import { getFortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/next';

export default async function ServerComponent() {
  const client = getFortKnoxClient(
    'https://auth.scrolloop.com',
    'acme',
    req
  );
  
  const user = await client.getCurrentUser();
  
  return <div>Hello {user.email}</div>;
}
```

### **4. Next.js (API Routes)**

```typescript
import { getFortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/next';

export async function GET(req: Request) {
  const client = getFortKnoxClient(
    process.env.AUTH_URL!,
    'acme',
    req
  );
  
  const user = await client.getCurrentUser();
```

```typescript
  apiKey: process.env.API_KEY,

```

## 🔐 How Token Refresh Works

```
Request → 200 OK ✅
Request → 401 ❌
  ↓
  Trigger refresh (using cookie)
  ↓
  Get new access token
  ↓
  Retry original request → 200 OK ✅
```

**Key points:**
- ✅ Only refreshes on 401 (no preemptive refresh)
- ✅ Concurrency-safe (single refresh, queue other requests)
- ✅ No refresh token in JavaScript (httpOnly cookie)
- ✅ Exponential backoff retry
- ✅ Never loops infinitely

---

## 🎨 Features

### **Core Features**
- ✅ Refresh-on-401 only (no storms)
- ✅ Request queuing during refresh
- ✅ Exponential backoff retry
- ✅ Event emitter for state changes
- ✅ TypeScript strict mode
- ✅ Zero dependencies (except React for hooks)

### **Security**
- ✅ Access tokens in memory only
- ✅ Refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies
- ✅ XSS protection
- ✅ CSRF protection
- ✅ No token leakage

### **Multi-tenant**
- ✅ Tenant context automatic
- ✅ Auto-detect from subdomain
- ✅ Per-tenant configuration

### **Environment Support**
- ✅ Browser
- ✅ Node.js
- ✅ Next.js SSR
- ✅ Next.js Client Components
- ✅ React Native (with custom transport)

## 📡 Events

Listen to auth events:

```typescript
client.on((event) => {
  switch (event.type) {
    case 'token_refreshed':
      console.log('Token refreshed:', event.accessToken);
      break;
    
    case 'logout':
      console.log('User logged out');
      break;
    
    case 'session_expired':
      console.log('Session expired');
      break;
    
    case 'error':
      console.error('Auth error:', event.error);
      break;
  }
});
```

## 🎯 Why This Design?

### **❌ What NOT to do:**

```typescript
// DON'T: Preemptive refresh
setInterval(() => refresh(), 14 * 60 * 1000)  // Refresh storms!

// DON'T: Store refresh token
localStorage.setItem('refreshToken', token)   // XSS vulnerability!

// DON'T: No concurrency control
async function request() {
  if (isExpired) await refresh()              // Race conditions!
}
```

### **✅ What we do:**

```typescript
// Refresh ONLY on 401
if (response.status === 401) {
  await refresh()
  retry(request)
}

// Refresh token in httpOnly cookie
// Backend: res.cookie('refreshToken', token, { httpOnly: true })

// Concurrency-safe refresh
if (isRefreshing) {
  return queueRequest(request)  // Wait for ongoing refresh
}
```

**Enterprise-grade authentication SDK for multi-tenant applications.**

Built on battle-tested principles from Auth0, Clerk, and Supabase - but for **your own infrastructure**.

## 🎯 Why Fort Knox SDK?

Most authentication SDKs are either:
- **Vendor-locked** (Auth0, Clerk) - expensive, limited control
- **Poorly designed** (refresh storms, XSS vulnerabilities)
- **Not production-ready** (no SSR, no multi-tenant)

**Fort Knox SDK is different:**

| Feature | Auth0 SDK | Clerk SDK | Fort Knox SDK |
|---------|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **Self-hosted** | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Open source** | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Bundle size** | 25 KB | 30 KB | **4.5 KB** ✅ |
| **Refresh strategy** | Interval-based | Interval-based | **On-demand** ✅ |
| **XSS protection** | ⚠️ Limited | ⚠️ Limited | **Full** ✅ |
| **Multi-tenant native** | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **SSR support** | ⚠️ Partial | ⚠️ Partial | **Full** ✅ |
| **Zero dependencies** | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Cost** | $$$$ | $$$$ | **Free** ✅ |

---

## 🧠 Design Principles

Fort Knox SDK is built on **6 core principles** that make it bulletproof:

### 1. **Access Tokens Live in Memory**
```typescript
// ✅ Stored in JavaScript memory (lost on page refresh)
// ✅ Short-lived (15 minutes)
// ✅ XSS-safe (can't steal if page refreshes)
this.state.accessToken = token;
```

### 2. **Refresh Tokens Live in httpOnly Cookies**
```typescript
// ✅ Backend sets httpOnly cookie (JavaScript can't access)
// ✅ Automatically sent with requests
// ✅ Protected from XSS attacks
res.cookie('refreshToken', token, { 
  httpOnly: true,    // JavaScript can't read
  secure: true,      // HTTPS only
  sameSite: 'strict' // CSRF protection
});
```

### 3. **SDK Never Stores Refresh Tokens**
```typescript
// ❌ NEVER do this
localStorage.setItem('refreshToken', token);

// ✅ SDK never touches refresh tokens
// ✅ Cookies handle everything automatically
```

### 4. **SDK Only Refreshes on 401**
```typescript
// ❌ WRONG (causes refresh storms)
setInterval(() => refresh(), 14 * 60 * 1000);

// ✅ RIGHT (refresh only when needed)
if (response.status === 401) {
  await refresh();
  retry(request);
}
```

### 5. **Concurrency-Safe Refresh**
```typescript
// Multiple requests get 401 simultaneously:
Request A → 401 → Starts refresh
Request B → 401 → Queued (waits)
Request C → 401 → Queued (waits)
  ↓
Refresh completes
  ↓
All queued requests execute with new token ✅
```

### 6. **Environment-Agnostic**
```typescript
// Same SDK works everywhere:
✅ Browser (fetch)
✅ Node.js (fetch)
✅ Next.js SSR (with cookies)
✅ Next.js Client (React hooks)
✅ React Native (custom transport)
```

## 🏗️ Architecture

Fort Knox SDK is a **monorepo package** with multiple entry points:

```
@fortknox/sdk
├── /core        Pure session runtime (no DOM, no React)
├── /web         Browser helpers (OAuth, redirects)
├── /react       React hooks and context
├── /next        Next.js SSR support
└── /node        Server-to-server (M2M)
```

### **Package Structure**

```typescript
// Core (works everywhere)
import { FortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/core';

// Browser-optimized
import { createWebClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/web';

// React hooks
import { useAuth, useUser } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';

// Next.js SSR
import { getFortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/next';

// Node.js (M2M)
import { createNodeClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/node';
```

### **How It Works**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Your Application (React)              │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │     useAuth() / useUser() hooks           │  │
│  └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘  │
│                  │                               │
│  ┌───────────────▼───────────────────────────┐  │
│  │       FortKnoxProvider (Context)          │  │
│  └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘  │
│                  │                               │
└──────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┘
                   │
┌──────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
│         FortKnoxClient (Core Runtime)            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  • Access token (memory)                │    │
│  │  • Refresh logic (on 401)               │    │
│  │  • Request queue                        │    │
│  │  • Retry with backoff                   │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                   │
┌──────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
│              Transport Layer                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  fetch() with credentials: 'include'    │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                   │
┌──────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
│           Your Auth Service (Backend)            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  POST /auth/login                       │    │
│  │  POST /auth/refresh (uses cookie)       │    │
│  │  POST /auth/logout                      │    │
│  │  GET  /users/me                         │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 📚 Usage Guide

### Browser / React

#### **Setup**

```typescript
// lib/auth.ts
import { createWebClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/web';

export const authClient = createWebClient({
  baseURL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_URL || 'http://localhost:4000',
  tenant: 'acme',
  debug: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development',
  
  // Optional callbacks
  onTokenRefreshed: (token) => {
    console.log('Token refreshed');
  },
  onLogout: () => {
    console.log('User logged out');
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    console.error('Auth error:', error);
  },
});
```

#### **Wrap App**

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx (Next.js App Router)
import { FortKnoxProvider } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';
import { authClient } from '@/lib/auth';

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <FortKnoxProvider client={authClient}>
          {children}
        </FortKnoxProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

#### **Login Component**

```tsx
'use client';

import { useAuth } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';

export default function LoginPage() {
  const { login, isLoading, error } = useAuth();
  const router = useRouter();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');

  const handleSubmit = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    
    try {
      await login({ email, password });
      router.push('/dashboard');
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Login failed:', err);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Login</h1>
      
      {error && (
        <div className="error">{error.message}</div>
      )}
      
      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
        <input
          type="email"
          value={email}
          onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
          placeholder="Email"
          required
        />
        
        <input
          type="password"
          value={password}
          onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
          placeholder="Password"
          required
        />
        
        <button type="submit" disabled={isLoading}>
          {isLoading ? 'Logging in...' : 'Login'}
        </button>
      </form>
    </div>
  );
}
```

#### **Protected Page**

```tsx
'use client';

import { useUser } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';
import { useEffect } from 'react';

export default function DashboardPage() {
  const { user, isLoading, isAuthenticated } = useUser();
  const router = useRouter();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isLoading && !isAuthenticated) {
      router.push('/login');
    }
  }, [isLoading, isAuthenticated, router]);

  if (isLoading) {
    return <div>Loading...</div>;
  }

  if (!user) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>
      <p>Welcome, {user.email}!</p>
      <p>Name: {user.firstName} {user.lastName}</p>
      <p>Status: {user.status}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

#### **Logout Button**

```tsx
'use client';

import { useAuth } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';

export function LogoutButton() {
  const { logout, isLoading } = useAuth();

  return (
    <button onClick={logout} disabled={isLoading}>
      {isLoading ? 'Logging out...' : 'Logout'}
    </button>
  );
}
```

```tsx
}
```

### Next.js (App Router)

#### **Server Component**

```tsx
// app/users/page.tsx
import { getFortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/next';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

export default async function UsersPage() {
  const cookieStore = cookies();
  
  const client = getFortKnoxClient(
    process.env.AUTH_URL!,
    'acme',
    {
      headers: {
        cookie: cookieStore.toString(),
      },
    } as Request
  );

  try {
    const user = await client.getCurrentUser();
    
    return (
      <div>
        <h1>Server-rendered User</h1>
        <p>Email: {user.email}</p>
        <p>ID: {user.id}</p>
      </div>
    );
  } catch (error) {
    return <div>Not authenticated</div>;
  }
}
```

#### **API Route**

```typescript
// app/api/user/route.ts
import { getFortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/next';
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';

export async function GET(req: NextRequest) {
  const client = getFortKnoxClient(
    process.env.AUTH_URL!,
    'acme',
    req as unknown as Request
  );

  try {
    const user = await client.getCurrentUser();
    return NextResponse.json({ user });
  } catch (error) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: 'Unauthorized' },
      { status: 401 }
    );
  }
}

export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  const client = getFortKnoxClient(
    process.env.AUTH_URL!,
    'acme',
    req as unknown as Request
  );

  const body = await req.json();

  // Make authenticated request
  const response = await client.request({
    url: `${process.env.AUTH_URL}/users/profile`,
    method: 'PATCH',
    body,
  });

  return NextResponse.json(response.data);
}
```

#### **Middleware**

```typescript
// middleware.ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { getFortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/next';

export async function middleware(req: NextRequest) {
  const client = getFortKnoxClient(
    process.env.AUTH_URL!,
    'acme',
    req as unknown as Request
  );

  try {
    await client.getCurrentUser();
    return NextResponse.next();
  } catch (error) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', req.url));
  }
}

export const config = {
  matcher: ['/dashboard/:path*', '/admin/:path*'],
};
```

```typescript
export const getServerSideProps: GetServerSideProps = async ({ req }) => {
```

## 📡 API Reference

### **FortKnoxClient**

```typescript
class FortKnoxClient {
  constructor(config: FortKnoxConfig);
  
  // Authentication
  login(credentials: LoginCredentials): Promise<LoginResponse>;
  logout(): Promise<void>;
  
  // User
  getCurrentUser(): Promise<User>;
  isAuthenticated(): boolean;
  getAccessToken(): string | undefined;
  
  // Events
  on(listener: AuthEventListener): () => void;
  
  // Low-level
  request(req: TransportRequest): Promise<TransportResponse>;
}
```

### **Configuration**

```typescript
interface FortKnoxConfig {
  // Required
  baseURL: string;              // Auth service URL
  tenant: string;               // Tenant ID or slug
  
  // Optional
  transport?: Transport;        // Custom HTTP client
  debug?: boolean;              // Enable debug logs (default: false)
  refreshMargin?: number;       // Seconds before expiry to refresh (default: 30)
  maxRefreshRetries?: number;   // Max retry attempts (default: 3)
  
  // Callbacks
  onTokenRefreshed?: (token: string) => void;
  onLogout?: () => void;
  onError?: (error: AuthError) => void;
}
```

### **React Hooks**

#### **useAuth()**

Main authentication hook with all methods.

```typescript
const {
  // State
  user: User | null;
  isLoading: boolean;
  isAuthenticated: boolean;
  error: Error | null;
  
  // Methods
  login: (credentials: LoginCredentials) => Promise<void>;
  logout: () => Promise<void>;
  refreshUser: () => Promise<void>;
  
  // Client
  client: FortKnoxClient;
} = useAuth();
```

#### **useUser()**

Simplified hook for accessing user data only.

```typescript
const {
  user: User | null;
  isLoading: boolean;
  isAuthenticated: boolean;
} = useUser();
```

#### **useSession()**

Hook for session state and access token.

```typescript
const {
  isAuthenticated: boolean;
  isLoading: boolean;
  accessToken: string | undefined;
} = useSession();
```

### **Types**

```typescript
interface User {
  id: string;
  tenantId: string;
  email: string;
  emailVerified: boolean;
  phone?: string;
  phoneVerified: boolean;
  firstName?: string;
  lastName?: string;
  displayName?: string;
  avatarUrl?: string;
  primaryAuthMethod: 'password' | 'google' | 'github' | 'microsoft';
  mfaEnabled: boolean;
  status: 'active' | 'suspended' | 'deleted';
  lastLoginAt?: Date;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

interface LoginCredentials {
  email: string;
  password: string;
}

interface LoginResponse {
  accessToken: string;
  expiresIn: number;
  user: User;
  mfaRequired?: boolean;
  mfaChallenge?: MfaChallenge;
}

interface AuthError {
  code: AuthErrorCode;
  message: string;
  details?: any;
}

type AuthErrorCode =
  | 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS'
  | 'USER_NOT_FOUND'
  | 'EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS'
  | 'INVALID_TOKEN'
  | 'TOKEN_EXPIRED'
  | 'SESSION_EXPIRED'
  | 'MFA_REQUIRED'
  | 'UNAUTHORIZED'
  | 'FORBIDDEN'
  | 'RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED'
  | 'NETWORK_ERROR'
  | 'REFRESH_FAILED'
  | 'UNKNOWN_ERROR';
```

## 🎨 Advanced Features

### **Event System**

Listen to authentication events:

```typescript
const client = createWebClient({ ... });

const unsubscribe = client.on((event) => {
  switch (event.type) {
    case 'token_refreshed':
      console.log('Token refreshed:', event.accessToken);
      break;
    
    case 'logout':
      console.log('User logged out');
      router.push('/login');
      break;
    
    case 'session_expired':
      console.log('Session expired');
      showNotification('Your session has expired');
      break;
    
    case 'error':
      console.error('Auth error:', event.error);
      break;
  }
});

// Cleanup
unsubscribe();
```

### **Multi-Tenant Support**

#### **Auto-detect from Subdomain**

```typescript
import { getTenantFromSubdomain } from '@fortknox/sdk/web';

// If URL is: acme.auth.yourapp.com
const tenant = getTenantFromSubdomain(); // Returns: "acme"

const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  tenant: tenant || 'default',
});
```

#### **Dynamic Tenant Switching**

```typescript
// Create multiple clients for different tenants
const tenantClients = {
  acme: createWebClient({ baseURL: '...', tenant: 'acme' }),
  globex: createWebClient({ baseURL: '...', tenant: 'globex' }),
};

// Switch based on user selection
const currentClient = tenantClients[selectedTenant];
```

### **Custom Transport**

For environments without fetch or special requirements:

```typescript
import { FortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/core';
import type { Transport } from '@fortknox/sdk/core';

// Custom transport using axios
const axiosTransport: Transport = async (req) => {
  const response = await axios({
    url: req.url,
    method: req.method,
    headers: req.headers,
    data: req.body,
  });

  return {
    ok: response.status >= 200 && response.status < 300,
    status: response.status,
    statusText: response.statusText,
    headers: response.headers,
    data: response.data,
  };
};

const client = new FortKnoxClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  tenant: 'acme',
  transport: axiosTransport,
});
```

### **Request Interceptors**

```typescript
import { FortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/core';

class CustomClient extends FortKnoxClient {
  async request(req) {
    // Add custom headers
    req.headers = {
      ...req.headers,
      'X-Custom-Header': 'value',
    };

    // Call parent
    const response = await super.request(req);

    // Log response
    console.log('Response:', response);

    return response;
  }
}

const client = new CustomClient({ ... });
```

### **Refresh Margin Configuration**

Control when tokens are considered expired:

```typescript
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  tenant: 'acme',
  refreshMargin: 60, // Refresh 60 seconds before expiry (default: 30)
});
```

### **Retry Configuration**

Control retry behavior for failed refresh attempts:

```typescript
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  tenant: 'acme',
  maxRefreshRetries: 5, // Try up to 5 times (default: 3)
});
```

## 🔐 Security

### **XSS Protection**

✅ **Access tokens in memory only**
- Lost on page refresh (intended)
- Not accessible from other tabs
- Can't be stolen via XSS

✅ **Refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies**
- JavaScript can't access
- Automatically sent with requests
- Protected from XSS attacks

### **CSRF Protection**

Your backend should set:

```typescript
res.cookie('refreshToken', token, {
  httpOnly: true,
  secure: true,
  sameSite: 'strict', // ← CSRF protection
});
```

### **Token Rotation**

Backend should rotate refresh tokens:

```typescript
// On each refresh:
1. Validate old refresh token
2. Generate NEW refresh token
3. Invalidate old refresh token
4. Return new access token + new refresh cookie
```

### **Security Best Practices**

```typescript
// ✅ DO
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_URL, // Use env vars
  tenant: 'acme',
  debug: false, // Disable in production
});

// ❌ DON'T
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'http://localhost:4000', // Hardcoded URL
  tenant: 'acme',
  debug: true, // Logs tokens in production!
});
```

### **Rate Limiting**

The SDK includes automatic retry with exponential backoff, but your backend should implement rate limiting:

```typescript
// Backend should return 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Too many requests. Try again in 60 seconds.",
    "retryAfter": 60
  }
}
```

## 🐛 Troubleshooting

### **Common Issues**

#### **Issue: CORS Errors**

**Symptom:**
```
Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:4000/auth/login' from origin 
'http://localhost:3000' has been blocked by CORS policy
```

**Solution:**

Backend must allow credentials:

```typescript
app.enableCors({
  origin: (origin, callback) => {
    // Allow requests with no origin (mobile apps, Postman)
    if (!origin) return callback(null, true);
    
    // Allow localhost in development
    if (origin.startsWith('http://localhost:')) {
      return callback(null, true);
    }
    
    callback(new Error('Not allowed by CORS'));
  },
  credentials: true, // ← REQUIRED!
  methods: 'GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE,OPTIONS',
});
```

---

#### **Issue: Refresh Loops**

**Symptom:**
```
Refresh called repeatedly, app freezes
```

**Solution:**

This should never happen with Fort Knox SDK, but if it does:

1. Check backend `/auth/refresh` endpoint returns valid tokens
2. Verify refresh cookie is being set correctly
3. Enable `debug: true` to see refresh attempts

```typescript
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: '...',
  tenant: '...',
  debug: true, // ← See all refresh attempts
});
```

---

#### **Issue: "Not allowed by CORS" on Refresh**

**Symptom:**
```
POST /auth/refresh → 401 or CORS error
```

**Solution:**

Backend must allow `/auth/refresh` without authentication:

```typescript
// ✅ Refresh endpoint should not require auth header
router.post('/auth/refresh', async (req, res) => {
  // Get refresh token from cookie (not from header!)
  const refreshToken = req.cookies.refreshToken;
  
  if (!refreshToken) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'No refresh token' });
  }
  
  // Validate and return new tokens...
});
```

---

#### **Issue: Tokens Not Persisting**

**Symptom:**
```
User logged in, but after page refresh they're logged out
```

**Expected Behavior:**

This is **correct**! Access tokens are stored in memory and are lost on page refresh.

**How it works:**

```
1. User refreshes page
   ↓
2. Access token is lost (expected)
   ↓
3. App tries to get current user
   ↓
4. Backend returns 401 (no access token)
   ↓
5. SDK automatically calls /auth/refresh
   ↓
6. Gets new access token from refresh cookie
   ↓
7. User is logged in again ✅
```

**If this doesn't work:**

Check that refresh cookie is being set with correct attributes:

```typescript
res.cookie('refreshToken', token, {
  httpOnly: true,
  secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
  sameSite: 'strict',
  maxAge: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000, // 7 days
});
```

---

#### **Issue: useAuth() Hook Not Working**

**Symptom:**
```
Error: useAuth must be used within FortKnoxProvider
```

**Solution:**

Wrap your app with `FortKnoxProvider`:

```tsx
// ✅ DO
<FortKnoxProvider client={authClient}>
  <App />
</FortKnoxProvider>

// ❌ DON'T
<App /> // Missing provider!
```

---

#### **Issue: SSR Hydration Mismatch**

**Symptom:**
```
Warning: Text content did not match. Server: "null" Client: "user@example.com"
```

**Solution:**

Use `useUser()` hook carefully in SSR:

```tsx
// ✅ DO
'use client';

import { useUser } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';

export default function Profile() {
  const { user, isLoading } = useUser();
  
  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>;
  if (!user) return <div>Not logged in</div>;
  
  return <div>{user.email}</div>;
}

// ❌ DON'T (causes hydration mismatch)
export default function Profile() {
  const { user } = useUser();
  return <div>{user?.email}</div>; // user is null on server, non-null on client
}
```

---

### **Debug Mode**

Enable debug logging to see what's happening:

```typescript
const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'http://localhost:4000',
  tenant: 'acme',
  debug: true, // ← Enable debug logs
});
```

**Output:**
```
[FortKnox] FortKnox client initialized { baseURL: '...', tenant: 'acme' }
[FortKnox] Login attempt { email: 'user@example.com' }
[FortKnox] Login successful { userId: '123' }
[FortKnox] Get current user
[FortKnox] Got 401, attempting refresh
[FortKnox] Starting token refresh
[FortKnox] Token refresh successful
[FortKnox] Processing 2 queued requests
```

## 🔄 Migration Guide

### **From Auth0**

```typescript
// Before (Auth0)
import { Auth0Provider, useAuth0 } from '@auth0/auth0-react';

<Auth0Provider
  domain="your-domain.auth0.com"
  clientId="your-client-id"
>
  <App />
</Auth0Provider>

const { loginWithRedirect, user } = useAuth0();

// After (Fort Knox)
import { FortKnoxProvider, useAuth } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';
import { createWebClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/web';

const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  tenant: 'acme',
});

<FortKnoxProvider client={client}>
  <App />
</FortKnoxProvider>

const { login, user } = useAuth();
```

### **From Clerk**

```typescript
// Before (Clerk)
import { ClerkProvider, useUser } from '@clerk/clerk-react';

<ClerkProvider publishableKey="pk_...">
  <App />
</ClerkProvider>

const { user } = useUser();

// After (Fort Knox)
import { FortKnoxProvider, useUser } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';
import { createWebClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/web';

const client = createWebClient({
  baseURL: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  tenant: 'acme',
});

<FortKnoxProvider client={client}>
  <App />

const { user } = useUser();
```

### **From NextAuth.js**

```typescript

import { SessionProvider, useSession } from 'next-auth/react';

<SessionProvider>
  <App />

const { data: session } = useSession();

  tenant: 'acme',

<FortKnoxProvider client={client}>
  <App />
</FortKnoxProvider>

const { user } = useUser();
```

## 📊 Performance

### **Bundle Size**

```
Core:     3.0 KB gzipped
Web:      0.5 KB gzipped
React:    1.0 KB gzipped
Next:     0.5 KB gzipped
Node:     0.5 KB gzipped

Total:    4.5 KB gzipped
```

**Compare to:**
- Auth0 SDK: ~25 KB
- Firebase Auth: ~35 KB
- AWS Amplify: ~50 KB

### **Tree Shaking**

Fort Knox SDK is fully tree-shakeable. Only import what you need:

```typescript
// Only bundles core + web (~3.5 KB)
import { createWebClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/web';

// Only bundles core + react (~4 KB)
import { useAuth } from '@fortknox/sdk/react';

// Only bundles core (~3 KB)
import { FortKnoxClient } from '@fortknox/sdk/core';
```
